newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher, cash premiums strong.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher, cash premiums strong.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher with buying throughout the day fueled by forecasts for crop-damaging cold in the southern Plains and a sharp jump in cash spring wheat premiums, grain traders said.
Frigid weather was forecast for late this week from Nebraska to the Texas Panhandle, which meterologists said could damage the developing hard red winter wheat.

Also, railroads were suspending operations in flooded areas near Minneapolis which prompted a 10- to 25-cent-a-bushel rise in cash spring wheat basis premiums Thursday. Traders said the railroads' action curbed the amount of wheat for sale in the MGE cash market.
MGE spring wheat futures closed up 6-1/2 to five cents per bushel with May up 6-1/2 at $4.22-3/4. July was up 6-1/4 at $4.14.
Estimated wheat volume Thursday was 30.157 million bushels versus 21.846 million.
